name: Autarkic Field Engineering & Telemetry Suite
tag: Designs off-grid water, power and storage systems, then watches them from your phone.

scenarios.title: Size a solar and battery system
scenarios.ask: Size a solar and battery system for a {people}-person off-grid cabin with {days} cloudy day(s) of backup. Sun: {sun}.
steps: Estimated {=round(people * 2.3, 1)} kWh a day, peak {=round(0.6 + people * 0.625, 1)} kW, from typical appliances.
Chose {=round(people * 2.3 / (sun * 0.75) * 2, 1)} kW of panels, with a 2x winter margin, and {=round(people * 2.3 * days / 0.8, 1)} kWh of battery.
Added a ram pump from the creek: about 1,100 liters a day, no electricity.
Set phone alerts for battery under 30% and pump stalls.
followups: Why size the battery above the daily load?
The plan only uses 80% of the battery so it lasts longer. That is why {=round(people * 2.3 * days, 1)} kWh of need becomes {=round(people * 2.3 * days / 0.8, 1)} kWh of battery.
What does the phone app show?
Battery charge, solar output, pump strokes and tank level, with alerts you set. It works over Wi-Fi, cellular or a low-power radio link.
It is a planning estimate. A local installer should confirm wiring, code rules and site sun before you buy.

scenarios.title: Plan a micro-hydro site
scenarios.ask: We have a stream with {head} of head and {flow} of flow. What can a micro-hydro turbine give us?
steps: Logged {head} of head and {flow} of usable flow, leaving water in the stream for wildlife.
Power = 9.81 x head x flow x efficiency, about {=round(9.81 * head * flow * eff)} watts.
Sized the intake pipe to keep friction loss under 10% of head.
Added sensors for turbine speed, output and intake blockage.

result.title: Micro-hydro estimate
rows: About {=round(9.81 * head * flow * eff * 24 / 1000 / 9.2, 1)} (at 9.2 kWh/day each)

followups: Why is hydro better than solar here?
Hydro runs day and night, so {=round(9.81 * head * flow * eff)} W around the clock often beats a much larger solar array.
What if the stream drops in summer?
Enter the dry-season flow and the plan shows the low-season output. Most sites pair hydro with a small battery bank.
Often yes. Rules on diverting water differ by area, so check with your local water authority first.

scenarios.title: Design a water purification line
scenarios.ask: Purify {liters} a day from a {source} for the homestead and alert me if anything fails.
steps: Built the line from sediment and carbon filters to a final UV lamp, sized for {liters} a day.
Sediment filter changes every {=round(30000 / liters)} days at this flow.
Phone alerts for UV lamp failure, low flow and filter pressure drop.

result.title: Purification plan
rows: Lab test before first use, then yearly

followups: Is the water safe once this runs?
The design targets common risks, but only a lab test confirms it. The app reminds you when tests are due.
What happens if the UV lamp fails?
The app alerts you and can close a valve so untreated water does not reach the tap.
